reason: The single cited passage (E1) directly supports all key premises: it reports Hf-rich phase precipitation at interfaces, hindrance of grain-boundary sliding and dislocations, improved high-temperature strength/ductility peaking near 0.5 at% Hf, unchanged room-temperature performance, and no mention of density penalty. The evidence is accurately represented and specific to the proposed composition and mechanism.
premises: Hf addition (~0.5 at%) to a dual-phase RHEA promotes Hf-rich precipitates at phase interfaces
These precipitates hinder grain-boundary sliding and dislocation motion at high temperature
This improves high-temperature strength and ductility relative to the undoped alloy
Room-temperature mechanical properties remain essentially unchanged
Alloy density is not notably increased
